lessons.title: Outils d'artiste professionnel
lessons.oneGoal: Students will explore and safely use professional art tools

opening.activity: Mystery tool exploration: Show professional art tools (palette knives, brayers, fine brushes, sculpting tools) in covered containers. Students guess what each tool does. Introduce vocabulary: OUTIL (show tool gesture), PROFESSIONNEL (formal, careful handling), SÉCURITÉ (safe handling demonstration).

materials: Professional art tools (palette knives, brayers, detail brushes, sculpting tools)

closing.activity: Professional Artist Role-Play. Students choose their favorite professional tool and demonstrate proper use to 'art students' (classmates). Practice vocabulary: 'Cet outil professionnel fait...' Emphasize safety and skill.

troubleshooting.then: Tool study without handling: Use pictures and videos of professional artists using tools, practice vocabulary and safety concepts without physical tool use.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding that artists use special tools, like how doctors, builders, or chefs have professional tools

lessons.title: Mélange des médiums
lessons.oneGoal: Students will combine different art materials in single artworks

opening.activity: Show examples of mixed media artworks. Identify different materials used together: paint + collage, crayon + watercolor, etc. Introduce vocabulary: MÉLANGER (mixing gesture), MÉDIUM (hold up different materials), COMBINAISON (bringing hands together).

materials: Variety of art materials (paints, crayons, markers, collage materials, pastels)

closing.activity: Mixed Media Gallery Walk. Display all mixed media works. Students identify different mediums used in each artwork. Practice vocabulary: 'Je vois une combinaison de...' Discuss which combinations were most effective.

troubleshooting.then: Mixed media planning: Use magazines and art materials to plan mixed media combinations without creating full artworks, focusing on vocabulary and combination concepts.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Mixing different ingredients in cooking, combining different materials in building projects

lessons.title: Techniques de peinture avancées
lessons.oneGoal: Students will master advanced painting techniques beyond basic brushwork

opening.activity: Compare basic brush painting to advanced techniques using demonstrations. Show sponge painting, stencil work, palette knife techniques. Introduce vocabulary: TECHNIQUE (skillful gesture), ÉPONGE (dabbing motion), POCHOIR (stencil demonstration).

closing.activity: Technique Showcase. Students demonstrate their best advanced technique to classmates. Explain process: 'Ma technique avancée utilise...' Compare effects achieved with different techniques.

troubleshooting.then: Technique analysis: Study photos and videos of advanced painting techniques, practice vocabulary and technique identification without hands-on painting.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Watching house painters use different techniques, seeing how artists create different effects

lessons.title: Sculpture et modelage
lessons.oneGoal: Students will create three-dimensional artworks using various sculpting materials

opening.activity: Explore 3D vs 2D concepts using simple objects and pictures. Handle sculptures vs looking at paintings. Introduce vocabulary: SCULPTURE (3D gesture with hands), MODELAGE (shaping clay motion), FORME (outline 3D shapes in air).

closing.activity: Sculpture Gallery. Display 3D works so they can be viewed from all angles. Students walk around sculptures, describing what they see from different viewpoints. Practice 3D vocabulary.

troubleshooting.then: 3D construction with classroom materials: Use blocks, boxes, and other classroom items to explore 3D construction concepts and practice vocabulary.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Playing with playdough, building with blocks, shaping sand castles

lessons.title: Gravure et impression
lessons.oneGoal: Students will create multiple copies of artworks using printmaking techniques

opening.activity: Demonstrate concept of making multiple copies: stamp a simple design multiple times. Compare to unique artworks vs prints. Introduce vocabulary: GRAVURE (carving motion), IMPRESSION (printing press motion), MULTIPLES (counting copies).

materials: Printmaking materials (foam plates, cardboard, cutting tools)

closing.activity: Print Exhibition and Trading. Display print series. Students can trade prints with each other since multiple copies exist. Discuss how printmaking allows sharing artwork. Practice printmaking vocabulary.

troubleshooting.then: Print analysis and planning: Study different types of prints, plan printmaking designs on paper, practice vocabulary without actual printing process.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Stamps, copying machines, printed books and newspapers

lessons.title: Collage sophistiqué
lessons.oneGoal: Students will create complex collages using advanced layering and composition

opening.activity: Compare simple collages to sophisticated examples. Identify layers, composition principles, intentional material choices. Introduce vocabulary: COLLAGE (layering gesture), COUCHE (layer-building motion), COMPOSITION (arranging gesture).

materials: Variety of sophisticated collage materials (textured papers, transparencies, fabrics)

closing.activity: Collage Critique Session. Students present their sophisticated collages, explaining layering and compositional choices. Use advanced vocabulary: 'Ma composition utilise des couches pour...'

troubleshooting.then: Collage analysis and planning: Study sophisticated collages in art books or online, plan complex collages on paper using drawing and vocabulary practice.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Magazine layouts, scrapbooks, mood boards, advertising design

lessons.title: Art textile
lessons.oneGoal: Students will explore fiber arts including weaving, stitching, and fabric manipulation

opening.activity: Explore different textiles: woven vs knitted vs sewn. Feel different fabric textures and structures. Introduce vocabulary: TEXTILE (fabric touching motion), TISSER (weaving motion with fingers), COUDRE (stitching motion).

materials: Simple weaving looms or cardboard frames

closing.activity: Textile Arts Appreciation. Display textile creations and discuss how textile arts connect to clothing, decoration, and cultural traditions. Practice textile vocabulary in context.

troubleshooting.then: Textile exploration without tools: Examine different fabrics and textiles, practice vocabulary, plan textile art projects using drawing and fabric samples.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Clothing construction, quilts, traditional crafts, home decoration

lessons.title: Techniques mixtes
lessons.oneGoal: Students will combine multiple advanced techniques in single complex artworks

opening.activity: Review all advanced techniques learned in previous lessons. Show examples of artworks combining multiple techniques. Introduce vocabulary: MIXTE (combining gesture), COMPLEXE (layered complexity gesture), INTÉGRER (integration motion).

materials: All materials from previous advanced technique lessons

closing.activity: Complex Artwork Presentation. Students present their multi-technique works, explaining how different techniques were integrated. Use sophisticated vocabulary to describe complex creative decisions.

troubleshooting.then: Integration planning and analysis: Plan multi-technique artworks on paper, analyze complex artworks by other artists, practice integration vocabulary without full creation.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Professional artists combining many techniques, complex craft projects

lessons.title: Style personnel avancé
lessons.oneGoal: Students will develop and articulate their own advanced artistic style

opening.activity: Look at students' artwork from throughout the unit. Identify patterns in their choices: favorite techniques, colors, subjects, approaches. Introduce vocabulary: STYLE (distinctive gesture), PERSONNEL (point to self), DÉVELOPPER (growth motion).

materials: Student artwork portfolios from entire unit
Art creation materials matching individual preferences

closing.activity: Personal Style Gallery. Display newest artworks that emphasize individual styles. Students present style statements and point out style elements in their work. Celebrate artistic individuality.

troubleshooting.then: Style study without creation: Analyze famous artists' styles, identify style elements in artwork reproduction, practice style vocabulary through analysis activities.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Recognizing that everyone has their own way of creating and expressing

lessons.title: Art conceptuel
lessons.oneGoal: Students will create artworks that express specific ideas or concepts

opening.activity: Discuss difference between decorative art and conceptual art. Show examples of art that expresses ideas vs art that's purely visual. Introduce vocabulary: CONCEPT (thinking gesture), IDÉE (lightbulb gesture), EXPRIMER (expression gestures).

materials: All advanced technique materials from previous lessons

closing.activity: Conceptual Art Presentations. Students present artworks and explain concepts being expressed. Audience tries to 'read' concepts in artwork. Practice vocabulary: 'Cette œuvre exprime le concept de...'

troubleshooting.then: Conceptual planning without creation: Develop concept-to-technique plans on paper, analyze conceptual artworks, practice conceptual vocabulary through planning exercises.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding that art can express feelings, ideas, and messages

lessons.title: Critique d'art
lessons.oneGoal: Students will analyze and critique artworks using advanced vocabulary

opening.activity: Introduce art criticism as learning tool, not just opinion sharing. Practice constructive criticism vs destructive criticism. Introduce vocabulary: CRITIQUE (analytical thinking gesture), ANALYSER (close examination motion), VOCABULAIRE (words/speaking gesture).

closing.activity: Critique Reflection. Students reflect on criticism received and given. Discuss how critique helps artistic growth. Practice vocabulary: 'La critique m'aide à...' Plan how to use critique for improvement.

troubleshooting.then: Critique practice with reproductions: Practice critique skills using famous artworks or art reproductions, focusing on vocabulary development and analytical thinking.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Discussing movies, books, music - expressing opinions about creative works

lessons.title: Processus créatif
lessons.oneGoal: Students will understand and document their own creative process

opening.activity: Discuss how they created their best artwork: what steps, what decisions, what changes. Introduce vocabulary: PROCESSUS (step-by-step motion), CRÉATIF (creative thinking gesture), DOCUMENTER (recording/writing motion).

closing.activity: Process Sharing. Students share insights about their creative processes. Compare different approaches. Discuss how understanding process helps improve art-making. Celebrate process diversity.

troubleshooting.then: Process analysis without new creation: Analyze creative processes used in previous artworks, discuss creative decision-making, practice process vocabulary through reflection.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding how they learn and create in all areas of life

lessons.title: Collaboration artistique avancée
lessons.oneGoal: Students will collaborate on complex artworks requiring advanced technical skills

opening.activity: Discuss how professional artists collaborate: sharing expertise, dividing complex tasks, combining different strengths. Introduce vocabulary: COLLABORATION (working together gesture), AVANCÉ (sophisticated level gesture), TECHNIQUE (skillful demonstration).

materials: All advanced technique materials from unit

closing.activity: Collaborative Artwork Presentation. Groups present artworks and explain how different advanced techniques were contributed by different collaborators. Celebrate successful artistic teamwork.

troubleshooting.then: Collaboration planning without creation: Plan complex collaborative artworks on paper, assign roles, practice collaboration vocabulary through planning exercises.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Professional artists working together, family projects requiring different skills

lessons.title: Installation artistique
lessons.oneGoal: Students will create large-scale installations using advanced techniques

opening.activity: Experience difference between small artworks and large installations. Walk through or around large classroom arrangement. Introduce vocabulary: INSTALLATION (environmental gesture), ÉCHELLE (scale comparison), ESPACE (space-defining gesture).

closing.activity: Installation Experience. Walk through completed installation as viewers. Discuss how large scale and spatial relationships affect artistic experience. Practice installation vocabulary.

troubleshooting.then: Installation planning and analysis: Plan installations on paper or in miniature, analyze famous installations, practice installation vocabulary through planning exercises.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Museum installations, public art, themed room decoration

lessons.title: Maîtrise technique
lessons.oneGoal: Students will demonstrate mastery of chosen advanced techniques

opening.activity: Review all advanced techniques learned in unit. Students identify which techniques they feel most confident using. Introduce vocabulary: MAÎTRISE (mastery demonstration), DÉMONTRER (showing/proving gesture), CHOISI (choice-making gesture).

materials: High-quality art materials for mastery work

closing.activity: Mastery Exhibition. Present mastery artworks with formal artist statements. Celebrate individual technical growth and achievement. Practice mastery vocabulary in formal presentation context.

troubleshooting.then: Mastery planning and analysis: Plan mastery demonstrations on paper, analyze technical mastery in professional artworks, practice mastery vocabulary through self-assessment.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Showing what they've learned, like performing a piano piece or demonstrating sports skills
